newsitem.title: USA: Ex FDA chief wants part of tobacco deal rewritten.
newsitem.headline: Ex FDA chief wants part of tobacco deal rewritten.

text.p: Former Food and Drug Administration chief David Kessler said Sunday several elements of the deal between tobacco companies and state attorneys general needed to be rewritten.

Interviewed on NBC's "Meet The Press," Kessler said the agreement actually diminished the ability of the FDA to control the amount of nicotine in cigarettes, which had been confirmed by the legal system.
"There are a lot of hurdles for the FDA, some impossible burdens," Kessler said.
"This document has a lot of legal terms and ... this seems to be a step back," he said.

Kessler was not involved in the deal but is considered a very influential voice since he spearheaded FDA efforts to regulate tobacco. The White House has said it would consult him before deciding whether to support the settlement.
"I'd like to see a resolution and I certainly support some of the elements but other elements have to be rewritten," Kessler said of the settlement which was announced Friday.
"This settlement is asking the industry to do something it would not naturally do -- sell fewer cigarettes to people. And if you look at the penalties, I don't think they're strong enough," he said.
He said Congress and the White House needed to examine the agreement carefully and not rubber stamp it.
"I think everybody needs to go slow, look at the details. I'm in favor of a resolution but we just have to think this one through," said Kessler.
